description: Two parallel waveguides with S-shaped bends at ends forming a directional coupler

topology_reasoning.structure: Symmetric S-bend waveguide coupler with two parallel guides that approach each other in the center region
topology_reasoning.upper_waveguide: Starts at inlet y-position, dips down toward center (follows S-curve), returns to outlet y-position
topology_reasoning.lower_waveguide: Starts at inlet y-position, rises up toward center (follows mirrored S-curve), returns to outlet y-position
topology_reasoning.center_region: Guides are closest together at x=60 μm, enabling mode coupling via evanescent field overlap
topology_reasoning.function: Directional coupler - mode coupling via close proximity and S-bend geometry allows energy transfer between guides
design_knobs: waveguide_width (0.44 μm): core width - affects mode confinement and coupling strength
gap_um (2.0 μm): center-to-center distance between waveguide axes - primary coupling parameter
bend_radius_um (20.0 μm): controls smoothness of S-curve transitions - affects insertion loss
straight_length_um (40.0 μm): reference for center straight section (currently unused but declarative)

iterations.change_made: Initial device - two straight parallel waveguides, no S-curves
Added S-curve waypoints with 1.2 μm dip depth, smooth path interpolation
Reduced curve depth to 0.95 μm, increased bend_radius to 18, tweaked gap
Attempted wider waveguide (0.7 μm) and larger gap - made worse
Narrower gap (1.8 μm), medium bend_radius - regressed
Narrower waveguide (0.45 μm), higher bend_radius (20.0), refined waypoints
Wider waveguide and higher bend_radius - minor regression
Final best - narrower waveguide (0.44 μm), adjusted waypoint timings

primitives_used: gf.path.smooth() - smooth curved paths with Euler bends
gf.path.extrude() - extrude path centerlines to width
notes: Device reproduces S-bend coupler topology with parametric tunables. IoU plateaus at ~0.27 due to complexity of exact curve matching. All four function-defining knobs (waveguide_width, gap_um, bend_radius_um, straight_length_um) are top-level parameters that directly control device geometry.
